Document: docs/CaliptraSSHardwareSpecification.md
Section: Manufacturer Control Interface (MCI) > MCI Feature Descriptions > Watchdog Timer
Section text (lines 1272-1290):


The Watchdog Timer within the MCI is a crucial component designed to enhance the reliability and robustness of the SoC. This timer monitors the operation of the system and can trigger a system reset if it detects that the system is not functioning correctly. The Watchdog Timer is configurable through CSRs and provides various timeout periods and control mechanisms to ensure the system operates within defined parameters.
The Watchdog timer contains two different timers. These timers can be configured in two different modes:

1. Cascade
2. Independent

In cascade mode when the first timer reaches a timeout two things will happen:

1. An error interrupt will be triggered
2. Timer 2 will start counting

If the WDT is not serviced before Timer 2 times out two things happen:

1. NMI output pin is asserted
2. NMI HW_ERROR_FATAL is triggered which can assert an error_fatal on the MCI port.

In Independent mode the two timers are completely independent of each other. When they timeout an error interrupt will be asserted. The NMI will never be asserted while in independent mode.

stimulus.text: Enable WDT timer1/timer2 timeout error interrupts and the MCI global error/notif interrupts.
Install the NMI handler address in the MCU NMI vector register.
Increment the reset counter to select the phase for this boot.
Phase 1: cascaded mode, wait for timer1 timeout, then warm reset.
Phase 2: cascaded mode, restart timer1, wait for timer1 timeout, then cold reset.
Phase 3: independent mode with both timers enabled, wait for both timeouts, disable each timer, then warm reset.
Phase 4: independent mode with both timers enabled, wait for both timeouts, then cold reset.
Phase 5: cascaded mode with a timer2 timeout, wait for the NMI pin in HW_ERROR_FATAL, then call handle_error if execution continues.
Phase 6: independent mode with timer2 enabled and timer1 disabled, set the timer2 period, wait for the timeout, then warm reset.
Phase 7: independent mode with T1_DIS_T2_EN, wait for the timer2 timeout, then cold reset.
Phases 8-9: configure cascade mode with a short timeout and issue a warm reset (8) or cold reset (9) during WDT operation.
Phases 10-11: configure independent mode with both timers and a short timer2 period, then issue a warm reset (10) or cold reset (11) during WDT operation.
Phases 12-13: configure independent mode with timer2 enabled and issue a warm reset (12) or cold reset (13) during WDT operation.
After all phases, signal test pass and halt.

Specification section: docs/CaliptraSSHardwareSpecification.md > Manufacturer Control Interface (MCI) > MCI Feature Descriptions > Watchdog Timer (lines 1272-1290)


The Watchdog Timer within the MCI is a crucial component designed to enhance the reliability and robustness of the SoC. This timer monitors the operation of the system and can trigger a system reset if it detects that the system is not functioning correctly. The Watchdog Timer is configurable through CSRs and provides various timeout periods and control mechanisms to ensure the system operates within defined parameters.
The Watchdog timer contains two different timers. These timers can be configured in two different modes:

1. Cascade
2. Independent

In cascade mode when the first timer reaches a timeout two things will happen:

1. An error interrupt will be triggered
2. Timer 2 will start counting

If the WDT is not serviced before Timer 2 times out two things happen:

1. NMI output pin is asserted
2. NMI HW_ERROR_FATAL is triggered which can assert an error_fatal on the MCI port.

In Independent mode the two timers are completely independent of each other. When they timeout an error interrupt will be asserted. The NMI will never be asserted while in independent mode.

Specification section: docs/CaliptraSSHardwareSpecification.md > Manufacturer Control Interface (MCI) > MCI Feature Descriptions > Watchdog Timer (lines 1272-1290)


The Watchdog Timer within the MCI is a crucial component designed to enhance the reliability and robustness of the SoC. This timer monitors the operation of the system and can trigger a system reset if it detects that the system is not functioning correctly. The Watchdog Timer is configurable through CSRs and provides various timeout periods and control mechanisms to ensure the system operates within defined parameters.
The Watchdog timer contains two different timers. These timers can be configured in two different modes:

1. Cascade
2. Independent

In cascade mode when the first timer reaches a timeout two things will happen:

1. An error interrupt will be triggered
2. Timer 2 will start counting

If the WDT is not serviced before Timer 2 times out two things happen:

1. NMI output pin is asserted
2. NMI HW_ERROR_FATAL is triggered which can assert an error_fatal on the MCI port.

In Independent mode the two timers are completely independent of each other. When they timeout an error interrupt will be asserted. The NMI will never be asserted while in independent mode.

relations.rationale: Configures independent mode with both timers enabled and polls WDT_STATUS T1 and T2 timeout bits. It services the interrupts but does not check that an error interrupt is asserted.
relations.missing: A check that the error interrupt is actually asserted (only the status timeout bits are polled).

relations.rationale: Phases 3, 4, 6 and 7 run independent mode with error interrupts enabled and wait for timeouts, but nothing checks that the error interrupt is asserted.
relations.missing: A check that the error interrupt is asserted on timeout in independent mode.

relations.rationale: Independent-mode phases run to timeouts, and the NMI handler would flag an NMI pin set. That check only reports and the test does not assert that no NMI occurs.
relations.missing: A failing check that the NMI pin and NMI output stay deasserted in independent mode.

relations.rationale: Phase 5 runs cascade mode with a timer2 timeout and polls until the HW_ERROR_FATAL NMI pin bit is set. The NMI handler is also installed.
Runs cascade mode with both timers timing out and the NMI handler tests the NMI pin bit. That check only reports, and there is no direct wait on or assertion of the NMI pin.
relations.missing: A failing check that the NMI output pin is asserted after Timer 2 timeout.

relations.rationale: Cascade mode with a T1 timeout, and the test polls the WDT_STATUS T1 timeout bit. It does not check that an error interrupt is triggered.
relations.missing: A check of the error interrupt itself.

relations.rationale: Phases 1 and 2 run cascade mode with T1 timeout and error interrupts enabled, then reset. No check that the interrupt is asserted.
relations.missing: A check that the error interrupt is triggered on timer1 timeout.

relations.rationale: Exercises independent mode with timer2 only and timer1 disabled, and both timers enabled. Nothing checks the independence of the timers.
relations.missing: Checks that each timer's behavior is unaffected by the other.

relations.rationale: Independent mode runs with both timers and the test polls T1 and T2 timeout status bits. It does not show that one timer is unaffected by the other.
relations.missing: A check that the timers do not influence each other, such as the effects of servicing one on the other.

relations.rationale: Phase 5 waits for the HW_ERROR_FATAL NMI pin bit after a cascade T2 timeout, which is observable evidence of NMI HW_ERROR_FATAL being triggered. The error_fatal output on the MCI port is not checked.
relations.missing: A check of the error_fatal output on the MCI port.

relations.rationale: Cascade mode with T1 timeout then T2 timeout and polling the T2 timeout status bit. This implies that T2 started, but it does not check it directly.
relations.missing: A check that Timer 2 begins counting right after the timer1 timeout.

relations.rationale: Phase 5 runs cascade mode to a timer2 timeout, which implies timer2 started after timer1 timeout. No direct check.
relations.missing: A check that Timer 2 starts counting at timer1 timeout.

relations.rationale: Configures cascade and independent modes across phases and runs them, but does not read back a mode setting.
relations.missing: Readback or verification of the mode configuration.

relations.rationale: Configures cascade mode and independent mode and observes different timeout behavior, without any readback of the mode configuration.
relations.missing: Readback of the mode setting and an explicit check of mode behavior differences.
